title: Supreme Court: Madison v. Alabama
summary: The Eighth Amendment may permit executing a prisoner even if he cannot remember committing his crime but it may prohibit executing a prisoner who suffers from dementia or another disorder rather than psychotic delusions. (No. 17-7505, opinion by Justice Kagan; 586 U.S. 265).

title: Supreme Court: Garza v. Idaho
summary: The presumption of prejudice for Sixth Amendment purposes recognized in Roe v. Flores-Ortega, 528 U. S. 470, applies regardless of whether a defendant has signed an appeal waiver. (No. 17-1026, opinion by Justice Sotomayor; 586 U.S. 232).

title: Supreme Court: Jam v. International Finance Corp.
summary: The International Organizations Immunities Act of 1945 affords international organizations the same immunity from suit that foreign governments enjoy today under the Foreign Sovereign Immunities Act of 1976. (No. 17-1011, opinion by Chief Justice Roberts; 586 U.S. 199).

title: Supreme Court: Nutraceutical Corp. v. Lambert
summary: Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 23(f), which establishes a 14-day deadline to seek permission to appeal an order granting or denying class certification, is not subject to equitable tolling. (No. 17-1094, opinion by Justice Sotomayor; 586 U.S. 188).

title: Supreme Court: Yovino v. Rizo
summary: The Ninth Circuit erred when it counted as a member of the majority a judge who died before the court’s opinion in this case was filed. (No. 18-272, opinion by the Court (per curiam); 586 U.S. 181).

title: Supreme Court: Dawson v. Steager
summary: By taxing the federal pension benefits of U. S. Marshals Service retiree Dawson, while exempting from taxation the pension benefits of certain state and local law enforcement officers, West Virginia unlawfully discriminates against Mr. Dawson as 4 U. S. C. §111 forbids. (No. 17-419, opinion by Justice Gorsuch; 586 U.S. 171).

title: Supreme Court: Timbs v. Indiana
summary: The Eighth Amendment’s Excessive Fines Clause is an incorporated protection applicable to the States under the Fourteenth Amendment’s Due Process Clause. (No. 17-1091, opinion by Justice Ginsburg; 586 U.S. 146).

title: Supreme Court: Moore v. Texas
summary: The Texas Court of Criminal Appeals’ redetermination that Moore does not have an intellectual disability and is thus eligible for the death penalty is inconsistent with Moore v. Texas, 581 U. S. ___. (No. 18-443, opinion by the Court (per curiam); 586 U.S. 133).
